name: Messer Truck and Van Maine, Messer Truck Equipment
old_description: Founded in 1899 by Walter A. Messer in Portland, Maine, we started as a one-man blacksmith shop building wagons, sleighs, and ship ironwork. As trucks replaced horses, we evolved into custom truck bodies and equipment, upfitting vehicles from the earliest days of motor transport. Four generations later, we’re still here doing what we’ve always done: building tough, work-ready trucks and vans, now as Messer Truck and Van.
about:
Messer Truck and Van operates from Westbrook, Maine, tracing its roots to 1899 when Walter A. Messer opened a one-man blacksmith and ship-smithing shop on Union Street in Portland. The family-owned business, now in its fourth generation, began by forging wagons, sleighs, and ironwork for ships before pivoting to truck bodies as motor vehicles replaced horse-drawn transport.

Today the company designs, installs, and services custom upfits for trucks and vans, handling everything from initial engineering through in-house installation and final inspection. Its two facilities—in Maine and Ohio—serve fleets ranging from a few work vans to full commercial operations, installing equipment such as aluminum and steel service bodies, crane packages, van shelving systems, and snow-removal gear. The shop also provides repair and warranty support for the products it installs.

Customers span construction, transportation, industrial machinery, and veterinary services, with documented projects for Maine Drilling and Blasting, Jewett & Noonan Transportation, WD Matthews Machinery Company, and mobile veterinary practices. The company also supports municipal and commercial fleets requiring consistent upfit specifications across multiple vehicles.

Messer emphasizes craftsmanship, clear communication, and a crew-first approach, values reinforced by its community partnerships with organizations like Westbrook Regional Vocational Center and STEAM Cathedral. Leadership continuity—Jeffrey Messer, the founder’s great-grandson, also served as NTEA president in 2015—underscores the firm’s deep industry ties.
